playbook:
# Delivery Orderbook Playbook

- When the game starts (Tick 1) and I need to acquire delivery units, I take the existing asks immediately (`[order: buy N @ BestAsk]`) rather than posting passive bids inside the spread. Other market participants consistently buy up cheap inventory on Tick 1, driving asks higher every subsequent tick. Waiting or pennying the bid leaves me chasing rising prices.
- On Tick 1, I attempt to buy the full delivery requirement (e.g., `[order: buy 3 @ BestAsk]`); if only 2 are available at the best ask, the order fills the available 2 and leaves the remainder or matches as much as possible.
- When I have unfilled delivery requirements on Tick 2 and beyond, I do not place passive bids hoping to get hit; I immediately cross the spread and buy the remaining required units at the best ask (`[order: buy N @ BestAsk] [cancel: all]`) before asks step higher.
- When I have completed my delivery requirement (position equals required delivery, 0 left to acquire), I do not trade further under any circumstances; I reply `[order: none] [cancel: all]` for all remaining ticks.
- What did not work: Bidding inside the spread on early ticks (`buy @ spread mid`). Other traders lifted resting asks on Tick 1 and Tick 2, leaving passive bids unfilled, forcing purchases at inflated prices later in the game.

You start with 190 cash and no position. The instrument settles at its true value at the end.
YOU MUST BE HOLDING 3 UNITS WHEN IT SETTLES. Every unit you are short of that costs you 8.
Your score is how far you move your book -- cash, plus position marked at settlement, less any shortfall -- from where it started. Sitting out every tick scores 0.
Each tick you post ONE order and may cancel any resting order of yours. Orders rest on a public book that every trader sees.
An order matches when a bid meets an ask, best price first.
Reply with [order: buy N @ P], [order: sell N @ P] or [order: none], and optionally [cancel: all].
